statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, define a mountain triplet of nums to be any triple of indices (i, j, k) such that 0 <= i < j < k < len(nums), nums[i] < nums[j], and nums[k] < nums[j]. If there exists at least one mountain triplet, then r equals the minimum of nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] over all mountain triplets; if there exists no mountain triplet, then r = -1.
preconditions: 3 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000000.

statement: Let rev(nums) be the array of length len(nums) defined by rev(nums)[t] = nums[len(nums)-1-t] for every 0 <= t < len(nums). Whenever the function returns a result r on input nums and a result s on input rev(nums), r = s.
preconditions: 3 <= len(nums) <= 100000; for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), 1 <= nums[i] <= 100000000.
